# Agastya: evidence graph, version 0.3

Research snapshot: 27 October 2026. 3295 nodes, 4199 claims, 105 sources, 13 chronological records.

Curated first-pass seed, not an exhaustive concordance. Translation checks and scholarly reports only; original-language philological review is pending. The expansion adds Vedic, epic, Tamil, and Buddhist reception links; it remains a sampled source review, not an exhaustive corpus census.

The five Agastya facets are source-local dossiers. Their labels organize traditions; neither one historical individual nor five separate people is asserted.

## Coverage and identity review

3101 named records have a checked textual passage; 10 more named records need primary passage review. The 3,000-record milestone is exceeded by 101 at the present review level. These are source-local textual entities, not a count of distinct historical people.

The Mahābhārata index contributes 2572 likely individual *candidate records* to a separate review queue; zero are counted before passage and identity review. Only 2078 exact spellings occur in this candidate stratum. See `progress.json`, `individuals.csv`, `expansion/inm-review.json`, and `expansion/INM-SOURCE.md`.

## Reading the graph

Arrows record passage-level claims, not established historical events. “Incoming” distinguishes a person speaking about Agastya from speaking to him. “Outgoing” includes attributed speech and is labeled where speaker assignments depend on interpretation. Geography distinguishes Agastya’s own words from descriptions by other speakers. Deities and personified places retain their entity types.

Most claims are checked against translations; selected Mahābhārata claims are checked against the electronic Sanskrit critical text. No systematic Sanskrit/Tamil philological audit or manuscript collation has been completed. Prose translation pages may interleave commentary: only translated narrative statements were used for primary claims.

## Principal findings

- Earliest textual horizon in this seed: the Ṛgveda; this dates attestations within a corpus, not Agastya’s lifespan.
- Ṛgveda 1.170.3 explicitly addresses Agastya. The Lopāmudrā dialogue requires editorial speaker assignments. Ṛgveda 7.33 places him in Vasiṣṭha birth imagery without identifying Vasiṣṭha as the speaker.
- Rāmāyaṇa 3.13 gives direct geographical speech about Pañcavaṭī and Godāvarī, and a claimed friendship with Daśaratha. Sugrīva’s Malaya statement is a different evidence type.
- Yudhiṣṭhira asks Lomaśa about Agastya; that exchange does not establish an Agastya–Yudhiṣṭhira meeting.
- Tamil commentary traditions connect Akattiyar with Tolkāppiyar and southern geography. Their primary passages remain to be audited. The Tolkāppiyam base text must not inherit its commentators’ claims automatically.
- Puṟanāṉūṟu 201 does not explicitly name Agastya. Mahadevan’s identification of its northern sage is retained as a hypothesis.
- No independently anchored birth/death interval for a historical Agastya is established by this dataset.

## Chronology

Calendar dates below belong to texts or witnesses unless explicitly marked otherwise. Narrative yugas and durations have not been converted into BCE dates. Alternative scholarly datings remain separate source-attributed claims.

| Claim | Type | Period | Source / qualification |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ṛgvedic textual horizon | text_composition | Latter half of the second millennium BCE | [Jamison and Brereton, The Rigveda (2020)](https://academic.oup.com/book/33632). Broad corpus horizon from Jamison–Brereton; not a dated birth, death, or individual hymn. Oral composition complicates finer dating. |
| Later Vedic reception | relative_textual | After the hymn tradition; absolute range not assigned here | [Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.5.5](https://sacred-texts.com/hin/yv/yv07.htm). Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.5.5 already treats a hymn as Agastya’s; a date for this particular layer remains to be sourced. |
| Contemporary of Rāma and Daśaratha | narrative_synchronism | Rāma’s exile; friendship with the preceding king | [Rāmāyaṇa 3.13](https://www.valmikiramayan.net/utf8/aranya/sarga13/aranya_13_prose.htm). Internal synchronism only. Does not independently supply a BCE year. |
| Tretā-yuga linkage | cross_text_traditional_placement | Tretā-yuga, through the Rāma synchronism | [Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.10.51](https://vedabase.io/en/library/sb/9/10/51/). Bhāgavata 9.10.51 puts Rāma’s reign in Tretā. Linking Agastya to it combines two texts; it is not an explicit birth date for Agastya. |
| Rāmāyaṇa formative period · Nagy synthesis | text_formation | Approximately 200 BCE–200 CE | [Gregory Nagy, Homeric Questions: comparison with Sanskrit epics](https://www-current.chs.harvard.edu/homeric-questions-2/). Broad scholarly model of epic formation; individual Agastya passages may have different histories. Earlier oral material and later growth are not excluded. |
| Past deeds in Yudhiṣṭhira’s narrative present | narrative_order | Earlier than Lomaśa’s account to the Pāṇḍavas | [Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Ganguli §96](https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m03/m03096.htm). The pilgrimage story establishes earlier deeds, not a meeting or a dated death. In §104 Agastya has not returned from the south as of the narrator’s present. |
| Nahuṣa’s curse | narrative_duration | 10,000 years in Ganguli’s Udyoga §17 | [Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva, Ganguli §17](https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m05/m05017.htm). The duration belongs to Nahuṣa’s serpent curse. It is not Agastya’s age and is not used as a calendar anchor. |
| Mahābhārata formative period · Nagy synthesis | text_formation | Approximately 400 BCE–400 CE | [Gregory Nagy, Homeric Questions: comparison with Sanskrit epics](https://www-current.chs.harvard.edu/homeric-questions-2/). Broad corpus formation, not the date of the war or the date of Agastya. |
| Bhāgavata · Holdrege’s dating | text_composition | 9th or early 10th century CE | [Barbara Holdrege, Mystical Cognition and Canonical Authority (2000)](https://academic.oup.com/book/2098/chapter-abstract/142029717). Numeric endpoints are visualization approximations to the source’s century wording. Applies to text, not narrated persons. |
| Bhāgavata · Ray’s older proposal | alternative_text_dating | 550–650 CE; published in 1935 | [Amarnath Ray, Bhāgavata Purāna and the Kārikās of Gaudapāda (1935)](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-the-school-of-oriental-and-african-studies/article/abs/bhagavata-purana-and-the-karikas-of-gaudapada/530F523DFEF6E24819E6D38249DCB079). Historical alternative in the dating literature; not represented as equal to a current consensus or as Agastya’s lifetime. |
| Nacciṉārkkiṉiyar commentary witness | commentary_attestation | 14th century CE in Zvelebil’s account | [Kamil Zvelebil, Pre-history of Tamil Literature](https://www.tamiluniversity.ac.in/english/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/paper_01-PDF.pdf). Dates this witness to the disciple tradition, not the origin of every Tamil Agastya tradition and not the life of Tolkāppiyar or Agastya. |
| Indus cultural-memory hypothesis · Mahadevan | interpretive_hypothesis | Post-Indus migration interpretation; no individual lifespan | [Iravatham Mahadevan, Meluhha and Agastya (2009)](https://www.harappa.com/sites/default/files/pdf/meluhha_and_agastya_2009.pdf). A modern interpretation of legends and undeciphered signs; no independently read Agastya inscription or secure absolute date is established. |
| Viṣṇu Purāṇa · Taylor’s tentative dating | text_formation | Possible present extent in 4th–5th centuries CE | [McComas Taylor, introduction to The Viṣṇu Purāṇa: Problems with dating](https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n8264/html/introduction.xhtml?page=5). Taylor calls this a reasonable guess, not an exact composition date. The genealogies are narrative attestations, not the lifespans of Nahuṣa or descendants. |

| MBA001 | Śeṣa · principal serpent · Ādiparvan 1.31 → is named as serpent child of → Kadrū · mother in Ādiparvan serpent genealogy | [Mahābhārata Ādiparvan 1.31.2–16](https://bombay.indology.info/mahabharata/text/UR/MBh01.txt). Pērāciriyar acknowledges a view that Tolkāppiyar followed other now-lost grammatical works, then argues that he was Akattiyar’s foremost pupil and followed his teaching. | scholarly_report. Reports a debate among commentators and scholars; it does not establish a historical teacher-pupil relationship. |
| TEX_004 | Pērāciriyar → attributes threefold tamil division to → Akattiyar · Tamil traditions | [pp. 10–11](https://www.tamiluniversity.ac.in/english/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/paper_01-PDF.pdf). Zvelebil reports Pērāciriyar’s attribution to Akattiyan of Tamil’s three divisions: iyal, icai, and nāṭakam; he also describes Akattiyam as the foundational text for Tolkāppiyam. | scholarly_report. These are statements attributed to the commentary, not surviving contents of a complete Akattiyam. |

| REX003 | Udāyin · Buddhacarita witness → addresses → The prince · Buddhacarita witness | [4.62–83](https://ancient-buddhist-texts.net/English-Texts/Buddhacarita/04-Book-IV.htm). ## Next research work

- Align all epic passages to the Sanskrit and the critical apparatus; preserve current edition-specific numbering.
- Audit the full Ṛgveda 1.165–191 attribution block and its named persons/places against an Anukramaṇī and a modern translation.
- Check Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1.2.2, Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 10.11, Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā 2.1, Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 5.16, Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2.7.11, Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 21.14; citations are leads, not verified graph edges.
- Read Tamil primary witnesses: Paripāṭal, Cilappatikāram, Maṇimēkalai, Vīracōḻiyam, Iraiyaṉār Akapporuḷ commentary, and Tolkāppiyam commentaries; source each date and variant.
- Expand Purāṇic coverage beyond Bhāgavata and distinguish unrelated works called Agastyasaṃhitā.
- Add Agastya/Canopus as a separate celestial entity after checking astronomical texts; do not infer a human lifespan from stellar visibility.
- Investigate whether the epic Trasadasyu is identifiable with Vedic attestations, without automatic name merging.
- Review manuscript witnesses, inscriptions, regional geography, Buddhist Akitti traditions, and Southeast Asian reception.
- Collate Bṛhaddevatā 4.55–64 against the printed scan and Sanskrit; the online transcription is marked unproofread.
- Check Puṟanāṉūṟu 201 in a primary Tamil edition and translation; keep its unnamed sage separate from Agastya pending that review.
- Compare the Buddhacarita 4.73 Sanskrit and modern translations before interpreting the Lopāmudrā clause.
- Search Mahābhārata and Purāṇa recensions systematically for further named relatives and interlocutors.
- Verify three-hop paths in alternate editions, especially the genealogy in Rāmāyaṇa 3.14 and the collective/individual Vasiṣṭha distinction in Ṛgveda 7.33.
- Scale entity review with the Sörensen Mahābhārata name index as a candidate queue; do not equate an index headword with a distinct person without passage and identity checks.

## Files

- `graph.json`: expanded nodes, source records, claims, and chronology.
- `seed-graph.json`: preserved initial curated graph.
- `people.md` and `people.json`: evidence dossiers for every person-like node.
- `progress.json`, `individuals.csv`, and `identity-review.csv`: counted dossiers, review levels, and same-name identity checks.
- `three-hop-paths.md` and `.json`: audited shortest paths through person-like claim endpoints.
- `force-graph-2d.html` and `force-graph-3d.html`: standalone Canvas force graphs with text witnesses, source links, and passage details.
- `force-graph-webgl.html`: alternate true 3D view using circular sprites and the locally vendored 3d-force-graph 1.80.1 bundle; `vendor/3d-force-graph-LICENSE.txt` contains its MIT license.
- `force-graph-three.html`: direct Three.js point-cloud view with circular sprites, bundled locally from `agastya-three-app.js`; `vendor/three-0.186.1-LICENSE.txt` contains its MIT license.
- `expansion/*.json`: reviewed research batches and review manifest.
- `claims.csv`: claims in a spreadsheet-compatible form.
- `chronology.csv`: narrative and textual chronology claims.
- `graph-fragment.html`: interactive view, intended for the Codex visualization runtime.

Regenerate with `python3 merge_agastya_expansion.py`, then `python3 measure_agastya_progress.py`, `python3 render_agastya_people.py`, `python3 render_agastya_hops.py`, `python3 render_agastya.py`, and `python3 render_force_graph.py`. `build_agastya.py` regenerates the original seed.

To rebuild the direct Three.js bundle after editing `agastya-three-app.js`, run `npm install` and `npm run build:three` from the project root. For the WebGL library view’s circular sprites, run `npm run build:webgl-sprites`, then regenerate the standalone pages with `python3 render_force_graph.py`.
